title: Confidentiality Marking, Identification and Reasonable-Person Tests
where_to_look: Look in the Confidential Information definition and the marking and disclosure procedures.
required: Require reasonable-efforts marking and identification, contemporaneous identification of oral and visual disclosures, written confirmation within 30 days, and a reasonable-person test.
fallback: Accept reasonable-efforts marking and identification if protection remains when the information’s nature or disclosure circumstances make confidentiality apparent.
escalate_if: Escalate any clause making a legend or timely confirmation a condition to protection or excluding oral, visual, observed, or inspected information.
flag_if: The clause makes a confidentiality legend a condition to protection.
The clause requires written confirmation before oral disclosures receive protection.
The definition excludes visual, observed, or inspected information.
The clause removes protection when marking or confirmation is late or absent.
The clause lacks a reasonable-person test tied to the nature or circumstances of disclosure.
preferred_language: “Confidential Information” includes information disclosed in tangible, oral, visual, observed, or inspected form that is marked or identified as confidential or that a reasonable person would understand from its nature or the circumstances of disclosure to be confidential; the Disclosing Party shall use reasonable efforts to mark tangible information as confidential, identify oral and visual information as confidential at disclosure, and confirm those disclosures in writing within thirty days, and failure to mark or confirm alone shall not remove protection.
confidence_note: Based on 7 findings across 7 counterparties, the direction is consistent but moderate, favoring reasonable-efforts procedures and reasonable-person protection.

Definition of Confidential Information — Oral Disclosures

title: Effective Date and Date Completion
where_to_look: Review the preamble, date line, execution provisions, and any commencement or retroactivity language.
required: Insert a complete, specific Effective Date and use it consistently throughout the agreement.
fallback: Accept the date of last signature as the Effective Date if clearly defined and all date placeholders are completed.
escalate_if: Escalate any retroactive effective date, pre-signing coverage, or conflict between the stated Effective Date and execution date.
flag_if: The preamble contains a blank day, month, or year.
The agreement uses an execution date without defining the Effective Date.
The Effective Date appears as a placeholder or corrupted text.
A provision applies confidentiality obligations to disclosures before the Effective Date.
Different sections state different Effective Dates.
preferred_language: This Agreement is entered into and effective as of [Effective Date] (the “Effective Date”).
confidence_note: Based on 9 findings across 7 counterparties, the findings consistently support completing or expressly defining the Effective Date, with limited variation concerning retroactive coverage.

title: Standard of Care and Protection of Confidential Information
required: Require the recipient to use at least the same care used for its own similar confidential information, never less than reasonable care.
fallback: Accept a commercially reasonable efforts or reasonable precautions standard, while retaining an affirmative duty to safeguard against unauthorized access, use, and disclosure.
escalate_if: Escalate any clause that eliminates an enforceable minimum reasonable-care standard or makes the recipient strictly liable for every loss or disclosure.
flag_if: The clause uses the recipient’s own-information standard without a reasonable-care floor.
The clause limits protection to disclosure and omits unauthorized access or use.
The clause imposes an absolute duty to prevent all loss or disclosure.
The clause allows representatives to access Confidential Information without equivalent confidentiality obligations.
The clause is grammatically incomplete or unclear about the operative care standard.
preferred_language: Recipient shall protect Confidential Information using at least the same degree of care it uses to protect its own confidential or proprietary information of like importance, and in no event less than reasonable care, to guard against loss, theft, unauthorized access, unauthorized use, dissemination, publication, or other unauthorized disclosure.
confidence_note: Based on 24 finding records across 15 counterparties, the direction is consistent toward an affirmative same-care standard with a reasonable-care floor, despite several malformed redlines.

title: Representative Access, Flow-Down and Responsibility
where_to_look: Representative disclosure, permitted-use, affiliate, and confidentiality flow-down provisions.
required: Require need-to-know Representatives to have written no-less-restrictive duties, with Recipient responsible for breaches and non-receiving affiliates excluded.
fallback: Accept equivalent existing written confidentiality duties instead of this NDA, while retaining need-to-know limits, breach responsibility, and the affiliate limitation.
escalate_if: Escalate if Recipient disclaims responsibility for Representative breaches or affiliates are bound without receiving the information.
flag_if: The clause permits disclosure to Representatives without a need-to-know limitation.
The clause does not require written confidentiality obligations for Representatives.
The Representative confidentiality standard is less restrictive than the NDA.
The clause does not make Recipient responsible for Representative breaches.
Affiliate obligations attach without requiring receipt or access to Confidential Information.
preferred_language: Recipient shall disclose Confidential Information only to its Representatives who have a bona fide need to know it and who are bound by this Agreement or by written confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those contained herein. Recipient shall inform each such Representative of the confidential nature of the Confidential Information and shall be responsible for any breach of this Agreement by its Representatives. No Affiliate of Recipient shall be deemed a Representative or have any obligation under this Agreement unless it receives or has access to Confidential Information from or at the direction of Recipient.
confidence_note: Based on 24 findings across multiple counterparties, the core controls are consistent, with repeated high-significance responsibility and affiliate-scope changes.

title: Require Reciprocal, Third-Party, Fault-Based Indemnity
where_to_look: Indemnification, defense, security-breach, and remedies provisions.
required: Require reciprocal third-party indemnity and defense limited to losses caused by the indemnifying party’s breach or culpable conduct.
fallback: Accept a reciprocal third-party indemnity tied to breach, with prompt notice, defense control, settlement protections, and an indemnitee-conduct carveout.
escalate_if: Escalate any unilateral or uncapped indemnity, first-party loss coverage, or indemnity for the indemnitee’s own misconduct.
flag_if: The indemnity applies to first-party claims or all losses without a third-party-claim limitation.
The trigger does not require the indemnifying party’s breach, negligence, or willful misconduct.
The indemnity is unilateral rather than reciprocal.
The indemnitee controls the defense or can reject settlements without settlement protections.
The clause lacks an indemnitee-conduct carveout.
preferred_language: Each party, as indemnifying party, shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other party and its affiliates and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, and representatives from third-party claims and resulting reasonable losses, costs, and attorneys’ fees to the extent caused by the indemnifying party’s breach, negligence, gross negligence, or willful misconduct. The indemnified party shall provide prompt written notice and reasonable cooperation and shall permit the indemnifying party to control the defense, but no settlement may impose liability on the indemnified party or fail to provide a full release without its written consent. This obligation does not apply to the extent caused by an act or omission of the indemnified party.
confidence_note: Based on 13 findings across 4 counterparties, with repeated patterns and consistently high significance.

title: Limit damages and preserve serious-misconduct carve-outs
where_to_look: Review limitation-of-liability, damages-exclusion, indemnity, and security-breach liability provisions.
required: Require a damages exclusion with carve-outs for gross negligence, recklessness, and willful misconduct, with losses allocated to the party causing them.
fallback: Accept a narrower damages exclusion only if it preserves liability for serious misconduct and does not shift losses caused by a party’s own fault.
escalate_if: Escalate any clause that protects a party from its own gross negligence, recklessness, or willful misconduct or shifts losses caused by its fault.
flag_if: The clause excludes consequential, indirect, special, incidental, exemplary, or punitive damages.
The liability limitation lacks a gross-negligence carve-out.
The liability limitation lacks a willful-misconduct or recklessness carve-out.
The clause assigns losses caused by the counterparty’s negligence or misconduct to Marmon.
An indemnity applies without regard to the indemnitee’s fault.],
preferred_language

Except for liability arising from a party’s gross negligence, recklessness, or willful misconduct, neither party shall be liable to the other for any consequential, indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, or punitive damages, including damages for business interruption, loss of use, revenue, profit, cost of capital, business opportunity, or goodwill, whether arising in contract, tort, or otherwise. Each party shall bear direct losses to the extent caused by its own negligence or misconduct, and neither party shall be liable for losses to the extent caused by the other party’s negligence or misconduct.
confidence_note
Based on 10 findings across 3 counterparties, with a consistent direction toward damages exclusions and serious-misconduct carve-outs.

title: Warranties, Disclaimers and No-Representation Provisions
where_to_look: Look in representations and warranties, confidential-information disclaimers, and as-is provisions.
required: Require a right-to-disclose representation plus an as-is disclaimer rejecting all other express and implied warranties.
fallback: Accept a disclaimer of accuracy and completeness with an express no-implied-warranties provision, but reject affirmative warranties about the information.
escalate_if: Escalate any affirmative warranty about the information or any disclaimer that omits the right-to-disclose representation.
flag_if: The clause warrants the accuracy or completeness of Confidential Information.
The clause lacks an express as-is statement for disclosed information.
The clause does not disclaim implied warranties or guarantees.
The clause contains an affirmative warranty beyond the right to disclose.
The clause imposes suitability, usefulness, or fitness obligations for the information.
preferred_language: Disclosing Party represents that it has the right to disclose the Confidential Information, but makes no other representation or warranty, express or implied, regarding the accuracy, completeness, suitability, or usefulness of the Confidential Information, which is provided “AS IS,” and disclaims all other warranties and guarantees, except for any express representation or warranty in a definitive written agreement executed by the parties.
confidence_note: Based on 9 findings across 5 counterparties, consistent direction toward broad disclaimers, with mostly medium significance and one high-significance change.

title: Equitable, Injunctive and Specific Relief
where_to_look: Remedies, equitable-relief, injunctive-relief, and specific-performance provisions.
required: Require an express, non-exclusive right to seek injunctive, specific-performance, and other equitable relief for breach or threatened breach without proving damages or posting bond or security.
fallback: Accept an express non-exclusive right to seek injunctive or specific-performance relief for breach, even if bond and damages requirements remain.
escalate_if: Escalate any provision that makes monetary damages the exclusive remedy. Escalate any provision that bars relief for threatened breaches. Escalate any automatic intellectual-property forfeiture for breach.
flag_if: The clause states that monetary damages are inadequate.
The clause authorizes injunctive or equitable relief.
The clause covers a threatened breach.
The clause waives proof of actual damages.
The clause waives a bond or other security.
preferred_language: Each Party acknowledges that a breach or threatened breach of this Agreement will cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages are inadequate, and the non-breaching Party shall be entitled to seek injunctive relief, specific performance, and any other equitable relief without proving actual damages or posting bond or other security, as non-exclusive remedies in addition to all remedies available at law or in equity.
confidence_note: Based on 14 findings across 12 counterparties, the direction is mostly consistent toward preserving or expanding equitable relief, with some negotiated deletions.

title: Governing Law and Choice of Law
where_to_look: Governing-law, choice-of-law, and related jurisdiction or venue provisions.
required: Require Delaware substantive law without regard to its conflict-of-laws provisions.
fallback: Accept another single U.S. state’s substantive law with a clear exclusion of conflict-of-laws rules.
escalate_if: Escalate any ambiguous, malformed, multi-jurisdiction, or non-U.S. governing-law clause before acceptance.
flag_if: The clause names two or more jurisdictions as governing law.
The clause changes the governing-law jurisdiction.
The clause lacks a conflict-of-laws exclusion.
The clause contains concatenated, incomplete, or malformed governing-law text.
preferred_language: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the substantive laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict-of-laws provisions.
confidence_note: Based on 38 supplied findings across 17 counterparties, governing law was consistently high-significance and repeatedly moved toward a clear U.S. jurisdiction with a conflict-of-laws exclusion, although the selected state varied.

title: Ownership, No License and IP Rights
where_to_look: Review ownership, permitted-use, no-license, and work-product IP provisions.
required: Require the discloser to retain all right, title, and interest in Confidential Information and related IP, with no license beyond Purpose-only use.
fallback: Accept a limited, express, non-transferable license solely for the stated Purpose, with ownership retained and IP filings barred.
escalate_if: Escalate any ownership transfer, broad or sublicensable license, unrestricted use, or IP filing right based on Confidential Information.
flag_if: The agreement does not state that the disclosing party retains ownership of Confidential Information.
The recipient receives a license beyond the stated Purpose or a right to sublicense.
The recipient may use Confidential Information in a patent, utility-model, or design-protection application.
A work-product assignment covers material created outside the recipient's contractual capacity.
The disclosing party may withhold consent to intellectual-property use without a reasonableness standard.
preferred_language: Discloser retains all right, title and interest in and to its Confidential Information, including any intellectual property contained or reflected therein or practiced thereby. Neither this Agreement nor any disclosure grants Recipient any right or license, express or implied, in Discloser’s Confidential Information or related intellectual property, except a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable right to use it solely for the Purpose. Recipient shall not include Confidential Information in any patent, utility-model, or design-protection application or otherwise use it for intellectual-property purposes without Discloser’s prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed.
confidence_note: Based on 11 findings across 8 requests, the direction is consistent on ownership and no-license terms, with moderate variation on consent and work-product scope.

title: Preserve Core Privacy Compliance and Incident Controls
where_to_look: Privacy, personal-information processing, security, incident-notice, and data-transfer remedy provisions.
required: Require compliance with applicable privacy laws, documented processing instructions, reasonable safeguards, prompt notices, and meaningful transfer remedies.
fallback: Accept a narrower law definition and reasonable safeguards with prompt incident notice, while retaining processing instructions and a contractual remedy.
escalate_if: Escalate if the counterparty deletes the privacy framework or removes processing instructions, notices, safeguards, or transfer remedies.
flag_if: The agreement does not define applicable privacy or data-protection laws.
The recipient may process Personal Information without documented instructions.
The agreement lacks a prompt Security Incident notice obligation.
The agreement disclaims the effectiveness of required security safeguards.
The agreement lacks a suspension or termination remedy for privacy noncompliance.
preferred_language: Recipient shall process Personal Information only on Discloser’s documented instructions and in compliance with all applicable privacy and data-protection laws, including the GDPR, CCPA, PIPEDA, and their implementing regulations, maintain reasonable administrative, technical, and physical safeguards, and promptly notify Discloser of any Security Incident, legally binding disclosure request, or request from a data subject; Discloser may suspend Personal Information transfers or terminate this Agreement for Recipient’s material failure to comply.
confidence_note: Based on 12 findings across 8 counterparties, the issue is consistently high-stakes and materially contested, with strong support for broad privacy obligations, processing controls, notices, safeguards, and remedies.

title: Venue, Arbitration and Jury-Trial Procedures
where_to_look: Governing-law, exclusive-venue, arbitration, and jury-trial provisions.
required: Require one clearly identified governing law and exclusive state or federal venue, with no mandatory arbitration or jury-trial waiver.
fallback: Accept a clearly identified non-exclusive state or federal forum under one governing law, with no mandatory arbitration or jury-trial waiver.
escalate_if: Escalate any mandatory arbitration, jury-trial waiver, unidentified forum, competing governing-law terms, or unapproved jurisdiction.
flag_if: The clause requires disputes to be resolved through arbitration.
The clause waives the parties’ right to trial by jury.
The clause names multiple governing-law jurisdictions.
The clause permits venue in any court with personal jurisdiction.
The clause fails to identify the city, county, state, or court system for venue.
preferred_language: This Agreement and any dispute arising out of or relating to it shall be governed by the laws of the state in which [Marmon-approved exclusive forum] is located, without regard to conflicts-of-law rules. The parties shall litigate any such dispute exclusively in the state or federal courts located in that forum, and each party irrevocably submits to those courts. Neither party waives the right to trial by jury, and no such dispute shall be subject to mandatory arbitration.
confidence_note: Based on 8 findings across 8 counterparties, all high-significance and actively negotiated, with varied forum outcomes.

title: Security Incident Notice, Containment and Remediation
where_to_look: Look in confidentiality, data security, notice, remedies, and incident-response provisions.
required: Require immediate notice of any potential or actual Security Incident, plus containment and remediation.
fallback: Accept notice without a fixed deadline only if it is without undue delay and the express containment and remediation duties remain.
escalate_if: Escalate any clause that limits notice to confirmed incidents or removes the duty to contain and remediate.
flag_if: Notice is triggered only by a confirmed Security Incident.
Notice is triggered only when a law requires notification.
The clause lacks an immediate or prompt notice deadline.
The clause omits an express duty to contain or eliminate the exposure.
The clause omits an express duty to take remedial action.
preferred_language: Upon discovery of any potential or actual Security Incident involving Confidential Information, Recipient shall immediately notify Disclosing Party and promptly take all reasonably necessary steps to eliminate or contain the exposure that led to the Security Incident and take remedial action in accordance with Recipient’s security incident management policies and procedures and all applicable Data Protection Laws and Regulations.
confidence_note: Based on 10 findings across 7 requests, the direction is consistent and high significance.

title: Reverse Engineering, Copying and Technical Use Restrictions
where_to_look: Confidentiality, use-restriction, copying, and intellectual-property filing provisions.
required: Prohibit reverse engineering and technical deconstruction, limit copying to the Purpose, and bar IP filings using Confidential Information.
fallback: Permit copies necessary for the Purpose, while retaining the prohibitions on reverse engineering and IP filings.
escalate_if: Escalate if the counterparty seeks a reverse-engineering right or automatic assignment of resulting intellectual property as a breach remedy.
flag_if: The clause permits reverse engineering, reverse compilation, decompilation, or disassembly.
The clause permits copying or transcription beyond copies necessary for the Purpose.
The clause permits Confidential Information to be included in a patent, utility-model, or design-protection application.
The clause assigns ownership of products or processes resulting from a breach.
The clause fails to treat permitted copies as Confidential Information.
preferred_language: Recipient shall use Confidential Information solely for the Purpose and shall not reverse engineer, reverse compile, decompile, disassemble, or otherwise seek to derive the Disclosing Party’s proprietary information or intellectual property from it, copy it except as necessary for the Purpose, or include it in any patent, utility model, or design-protection application filed by or for Recipient; all permitted copies shall remain Confidential Information subject to this Agreement.
confidence_note: Based on 7 findings across 7 counterparties, direction is consistent on core restrictions but mixed on copying mechanics and breach remedies.

title: No Obligation to Transact; Termination of Discussions
where_to_look: Review the no-obligation, transaction-process, and termination-of-discussions provisions in the NDA.
required: Require an express disclaimer of any obligation to transact and a right for either party to end discussions without liability, with confidentiality surviving.
fallback: Accept a clear no-obligation disclaimer and a right to end discussions on notice, with confidentiality surviving for the stated term.
escalate_if: Escalate any provision that makes ending discussions actionable before a definitive agreement is signed.
flag_if: The NDA states or implies that the parties are obligated to enter a transaction.
The NDA lacks an express disclaimer of any obligation to sign a definitive agreement.
The NDA prevents either party from ending discussions before a definitive agreement is signed.
Termination of discussions triggers liability or damages.
The NDA does not state that confidentiality obligations survive termination of discussions.
preferred_language: This Agreement does not obligate either Party to pursue or consummate the Potential Transaction or enter into any definitive agreement, and neither Party shall have any liability for deciding not to proceed. Either Party may terminate discussions and negotiations at any time by written notice to the other Party, without liability, provided that the confidentiality obligations in this Agreement survive through the end of the Term.
confidence_note: Based on 3 findings with consistent direction, with 2 high-significance changes and 1 moderate change.

title: Manage and Narrow Commercial Relationship Restrictions
where_to_look: Review non-solicitation, noncompetition, customer-diversion, similar-product, and residual-information provisions.
required: Require mutual, transaction-specific restrictions limited to direct solicitation of contacts known through the deal, with no general competition ban.
fallback: Accept a one-way restriction limited to direct solicitation of employees or customers learned through the deal for a defined period, while preserving ordinary competition.
escalate_if: Escalate any covenant that bans competing products or ordinary business, reaches unrelated affiliates or all relationships, or has no definite end date.
flag_if: The clause prohibits providing or selling competing products or services.
The clause covers parents, subsidiaries, affiliates, or related entities.
The clause applies to all employees, customers, or business relationships.
The clause bars indirect diversion, interference, or inducement.
The clause restricts employment or customer activity based on retained or residual information.
preferred_language: During the term and for one year after its expiration, neither party shall knowingly and directly solicit for employment any employee of the other party first learned of through the Potential Transaction or knowingly and directly solicit any customer of the other party with whom it had material contact through the Potential Transaction for the purpose of ending or materially reducing that relationship; this restriction does not prohibit general advertising, responses to unsolicited approaches, ordinary competition, the sale of competing products or services, or hiring a person who independently approaches the hiring party.
confidence_note: Based on 5 findings across 5 counterparties, the direction is mixed, with both narrowing and broadening of restrictions.

title: Independent Development and Similar-Product Safe Harbors
where_to_look: Look in independent-development, residuals, and similar-products provisions.
required: Require an express safe harbor for Receiving Party’s pre-existing, similar, and independently developed information and products, conditioned on NDA compliance.
fallback: Accept a narrower safe harbor covering only information or products developed without using or disclosing Confidential Information.
escalate_if: Escalate if the draft permits use of Confidential Information outside the NDA. Escalate if it rejects any independent-development safe harbor.
flag_if: The NDA lacks an express independent-development safe harbor.
The NDA prohibits products or services that compete with or resemble the Confidential Information.
The NDA treats possession or development of similar information as a breach.
The NDA permits use of similar information without conditioning that use on compliance with the NDA.
preferred_language: Disclosing Party acknowledges that Receiving Party may possess or develop information or products that are the same as or similar to the Confidential Information. Provided that Receiving Party complies with this Agreement, nothing in this Agreement restricts Receiving Party’s right to use or exploit such information or to independently develop, alone or with others, information or products for itself or others that compete with or are similar to products contemplated by the Confidential Information.
confidence_note: Based on 6 findings across 5 counterparties, the core pattern is high-significance and favors express protection, with one contrary deletion.
